subject: Private deployment — true-up mechanics, platform fee amortization & migration credit
messages:
From: Elaine Kwan <elaine.kwan@stratushealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@stratushealth.com
Date: Thu, 16 Apr 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment - true-up mechanics & bundled support credits

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our procurement team reviewed the RFP appendix and had a couple of follow-ups so we can finalize the SOW and move to internal approval:

1) Platform fee amortization — do you amortize the platform fee monthly over the committed term, or do you invoice it up front? Our finance team prefers amortization for capex budgeting but they want a clear schedule in the commercial terms.

2) True-up cadence — we deploy occasionally to accommodate seasonal load. What is Redwood's preferred cadence for true-ups (quarterly / biannual / annual)? Also are there soft caps or grace windows before additional capacity is billed?

3) Migration / implementation credit — the RFP asked for one-time credits to offset the migration effort. Can you confirm how those credits would be applied (offset against platform fee vs. invoice credit) and whether they are refundable on early termination?

We attached the Appendix that shows our expected baseline: 18 GPU nodes average, peak to 28 over a quarter. Please respond with a concise commercial approach so we can get internal buy-off.

Thanks,
Elaine Kwan
Sr. Procurement Manager
StratusHealth
Attachment: RFP-appendix.pdf
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Kwan <elaine.kwan@stratushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Apr 2026 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment - true-up mechanics & bundled support credits

Hi Elaine — thanks for the clear ask and the appendix. Looping in Marissa (AE) and Ben (Sales Eng) to put numbers against the options; Markus is on for any legal/commercial constraints.

High-level answers so procurement can proceed in parallel to a formal quote:
- Platform fee amortization: we can amortize the platform fee monthly across the committed term (typical terms are 12 or 24 months). We will include an amortization schedule in the SOW showing monthly P&L treatment.
- True-up cadence: standard is quarterly true-ups with a 30-day billing window after the quarter closes. If you prefer semi-annual true-ups we can do that, but the price per-node for longer cadence includes a modest risk premium.
- Soft caps & grace: we offer a 1-quarter grace buffer for first-year pilots (i.e., first true-up we hold to baseline +20% before billing), after which true-ups are applied per the schedule.
- Migration credit: we can offer a one-time migration credit that is applied as a credit against the platform fee invoices (not a cash refund). It is not refundable on early termination but can be applied to your final invoice balance.

I attached an initial pricing sheet with placeholders so Marissa/Ben can propose concrete numbers and trade-offs. If you can confirm target baseline (looks like 18 nodes) and desired term (12 v 24 months) we'll get a draft SOW and a DocuSign ready.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
Attachment: initial-pricing-sheet.xlsx

Hi Elaine — thanks for the appendix and Olga for the summary. Putting forward a set of concrete commercial options so your procurement group can choose a direction quickly. I'll keep the options compact.

Assumptions (please confirm): baseline 18 GPUs, expected average 20 nodes, peak 28; 1 year retainer unless you opt for 24 months.

Option A — 12-month commit (recommended for pilot):
- Platform fee: $120,000 annual (amortized monthly at $10k/mo)
- Migration credit: $20,000 one-time applied against platform fee invoices (applied over first 3 invoices as $6.67k reductions)
- Support: Standard (included) — business hours support + runbook access.
- True-up: Quarterly; first true-up holds to baseline +20% grace for first quarter. Overage billed at $1,250 per GPU-month above baseline.

Option B — 24-month commit (preferred if you want lower unit economics):
- Platform fee: $200,000 for 24 months (effectively $8.33k/mo amortized)
- Migration credit: $30,000 one-time (applied as credit against invoices)
- Support: Premier add-on $45,000/year for 24/7 SRE retainer (on-call, 2 on-site workshops/year)
- True-up: Semi-annual optional; overage billed at $1,100 per GPU-month. 10% discount on overage rate if you commit to 24 months.

Commercial flex: we can convert up to $25k of the migration credit into an implementation services SOW (if you prefer Redwood to run initial migration). That conversion just reassigns credit usage and does not change amortization.

Legal/commercial notes (Markus): we prefer non-refundable credits that can be applied to invoices; if Stratus insists on refundable credits we need a defined clawback formula tied to run-rate.

Next steps: confirm target baseline and term. If you want, we can draft SOW + DocuSign today and reserve the migration credit for 14 days.

Attachment: proposed-pricing-v2.xlsx

Marissa / Olga — thank you, that is helpful and much clearer. A few quick clarifications before we proceed to internal sign-off:

1) We will likely go with a 24-month commit to get the better unit economics. Please confirm the migration credit in Option B can be applied to the first 6 invoices rather than all at once — finance prefers smoothing credits across the first 6 months.

2) True-up cadence — we will accept semi-annual true-ups if you confirm the overage discount (1,100 / GPU-month) and the 10% discount on the overage rate. We also need a firm 6-month notice if we plan to exit, and confirmation that unused migration credit will remain as invoice credit to the final month (not refunded).

3) Premier support — finance is okay allocating budget for the Premier SRE retainer but they want a one-page deliverable list (on-call response SLA, on-site workshop schedule, quarterly advisory reviews) included as an appendix to the SOW.

If you can confirm the two items (credit smoothing and exit notice & credit treatment) I'll route to legal and we can get DocuSign executed. Prefer signing this week if possible.

Best,
Elaine Kwan

StratusHealth
